clf-avc-075.text: A company needs high-performance block storage for a latency-sensitive database running on Amazon EC2. The workload requires predictable IOPS and persistent storage independent of the instance lifecycle. Which AWS storage service is appropriate?
clf-avc-075.explanation: Amazon EBS provides persistent block storage for EC2 and offers volume types designed for predictable IOPS and low-latency transactional workloads.
clf-avc-075.hint: The requirement is persistent block storage attached to EC2.
optionRationales: EBS provides persistent block storage.
Instance Store is ephemeral local storage.
EFS is a shared file system.
S3 is object storage.

clf-avc-076.text: A media-processing fleet needs temporary very high-speed local scratch space that can be discarded when an EC2 instance terminates. Which storage option best fits?
clf-avc-076.explanation: Instance Store provides ephemeral storage physically attached to the host and is suitable for temporary buffers, caches, and scratch data that can be recreated.
clf-avc-076.hint: The data is temporary and can disappear with the instance.
optionRationales: Instance Store is ephemeral local storage.
EBS snapshots are backup artifacts.
EFS is persistent shared storage.
Deep Archive is long-term object archival.

clf-avc-077.text: Hundreds of Linux EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones must mount the same shared POSIX file system at the same time. Which AWS service meets this requirement?
clf-avc-077.explanation: Amazon EFS is a managed elastic network file system that can be mounted concurrently by many Linux clients across multiple Availability Zones.
clf-avc-077.hint: Think of the managed shared Linux file system.
optionRationales: EFS provides shared multi-client file storage.
EBS is block storage and is Availability-Zone scoped.
Instance Store is local to a host.
Glacier is archive object storage.

clf-avc-078.text: A company needs hybrid file access from on-premises applications using familiar protocols while storing data durably in AWS and keeping a local cache for low-latency access. Which AWS service is designed for this hybrid storage pattern?
clf-avc-078.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage services and supports hybrid file, volume, and tape use cases with local caching options.
clf-avc-078.hint: Think of the AWS gateway that bridges local storage protocols and cloud storage.
optionRationales: Storage Gateway provides hybrid storage integration.
EFS alone does not provide the same on-premises gateway and cache model.
Direct Connect provides networking, not storage semantics.
WorkSpaces is a virtual desktop service.

clf-avc-079.text: A company must transfer hundreds of terabytes to AWS, but the available network connection would take months. Which AWS service family provides physical devices for offline data transfer?
clf-avc-079.explanation: AWS Snow Family provides physical devices for large-scale offline or edge data transfer when network bandwidth is insufficient.
clf-avc-079.hint: Think of the physical AWS data-transfer appliances.
optionRationales: Snow Family supports physical data transfer.
Global Accelerator optimizes network traffic.
CloudFront is a CDN.
Transit Gateway connects networks.

clf-avc-080.text: A company needs a dedicated private network connection from its data center to AWS with predictable throughput and reduced dependence on the public internet. Which AWS service should it use?
clf-avc-080.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity from customer premises to AWS and can offer more consistent performance than internet-based connectivity.
clf-avc-080.hint: Think of the dedicated circuit rather than an encrypted tunnel over the internet.
optionRationales: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity.
A VPN traverses internet connectivity and can be more variable.
CloudFront is a CDN.
Snowball is a physical data-transfer appliance.

clf-avc-081.text: A company needs encrypted connectivity between its on-premises network and an Amazon VPC and wants a solution that can be established relatively quickly over existing internet connectivity. Which AWS service is appropriate?
clf-avc-081.explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates encrypted IPsec tunnels between customer networks and AWS over internet connectivity.
clf-avc-081.hint: The requirement is encrypted hybrid connectivity using the existing internet path.
optionRationales: Site-to-Site VPN provides IPsec tunnels.
Direct Connect is dedicated connectivity and may require physical provisioning.
Route 53 provides DNS.
Artifact provides compliance documents.

clf-avc-082.text: A growing enterprise has many VPCs and on-premises networks and wants a scalable hub-and-spoke architecture instead of maintaining a full mesh of individual VPC peering connections. Which AWS networking service should it use?
clf-avc-082.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway provides a centralized hub for connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks and simplifies complex network topologies.
clf-avc-082.hint: Think of the centralized networking hub for many VPCs and hybrid connections.
optionRationales: Transit Gateway provides scalable hub-and-spoke connectivity.
A full peering mesh becomes operationally complex as VPC count grows.
CloudFront is a CDN.
WAF filters web requests.

clf-avc-083.text: Two VPCs need direct private IP connectivity and the architecture is simple enough that a one-to-one connection is sufficient. Which AWS feature is the simplest fit?
clf-avc-083.explanation: VPC Peering provides direct private routing between two VPCs and is suitable for simple point-to-point connectivity.
clf-avc-083.hint: For only two VPCs, think of the direct peer-to-peer connection.
optionRationales: VPC Peering directly connects two VPCs.
Transit Gateway is valuable for larger hub-and-spoke topologies.
Internet Gateways provide public internet access.
Route 53 provides DNS.
